note: No member. A marker is kept by room AND member — a person holding one room as two personas keeps one for each — so the key holder never infers whose marker is meant.
A member that is not a DID.
No marker. A set says where the member has read to; there is nothing else for it to say.
A marker with no version. The version is what a reader that keeps a copy of the room counts against, and what orders two markers.
A negative version. `0` is the lowest: nothing in the room seen.
A version as a string. Markers are ordered by comparing versions as numbers; "9" would sort after "415".
A createdAt that is not an RFC 3339 date-time. It is the host's timestamp, carried exactly as the host returned it.
The message keys the member has read. A marker is a position, not a list of what was read: a list would grow with the room and would be a record of exactly which messages the member has seen.
When the member read. A marker carries where they read to, never when; a reading time kept beside it would be the reading pattern the key holder is forbidden to keep.
rewind: false. Only `true` is meaningful; `false` would be a second spelling of the default.
A request to share the marker — a read receipt. There is no such member: a marker is never sent to the room, its host or another member, so no request carries a destination for it.
Bare/unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced.
No marker. A set always leaves one in force, and the caller adopts it.
No `moved`. A caller retrying a request, or racing another device, needs to know whether this one moved the marker.
Which device set the marker. The key holder keeps no record of it, so a response has none to give.
